title: Mathlib v4.30 source proposition Nat.and_le_left
statement: The proposition declared as `Nat.and_le_left` in the pinned Mathlib v4.30 source.

evidence.checker_command: test "$(cargo run -q --release -p axeyum-lean-kernel --example nat_theorem_inventory -- land_le_left 2>/dev/null | grep -Ec '^Nat\.land_le_left[[:space:]]')" -ge 1
evidence.notes: `build_nat_prelude` admits `Nat.land_le_left` through the trusted `Kernel::add_declaration` gate. `nat_theorem_inventory`'s rendered type matches this fact's `formal.statement` up to variable naming. Anchored with `^Nat\.land_le_left[[:space:]]` so a sibling name cannot satisfy this row; `grep -Ec` consumes the pipe so the tested count decides the exit status. Run `--release` -- the debug build of this inventory example SIGABRTs on stack depth (unrelated to this proof). Mathlib's `&&&` (`HAnd`) for `Nat` is the SAME function as `Nat.land` -- `Init.Data.Nat.Bitwise.Lemmas`'s `Nat.and_*` family and Mathlib's own `Nat.land_*` family (already reconciled: F:ml430-nat-land-comm-7e6ad72e, F:ml430-nat-land-assoc-ad4775b8) state the identical proposition over that one function under two different pinned declaration names -- reconciling this `and_*` mirror to our `Nat.land_*` theorem is honest under the mirror-flip criterion in CLAUDE.md: Mathlib's `def` (`Nat.land`, reached via the `&&&` notation) is the same function ours proves the property about.

evidence.supports: land(5,6) = 4, strictly less than 5 -- a pair where land a b = a (submask degenerate case) would not discriminate a bound that is actually an equality in disguise.
axiom_footprint: [] -- the Nat prelude's trusted surface is empty
evidence.notes: `nat_axiom_inventory --require-axiom-free nat` enumerates the built Nat environment and exits non-zero unless it admits no Axiom, Opaque or Quotient declaration (measured: axiom=0 opaque=0 quotient=0). A theorem cannot depend on a trusted declaration the environment does not contain, so an empty trusted surface bounds `Nat.land_le_left`'s footprint by [].

notes: Proved in Axeyum by reconciliation with the already-proved `Nat.land_le_left` (`nat_prelude/rec_agreement.rs`, `declare_land_le_left_all`, predates this lane -- built to support `land_assoc`). Mathlib's `Init.Data.Nat.Bitwise.Lemmas` states `Nat.and_le_left` over the SAME `&&&`/`Nat.land` function, so this mirror flip is honest under CLAUDE.md's criterion. No prior ml430 mirror existed for `Nat.land_le_left` itself (Mathlib apparently only states this bound under the `and_*` name in this pinned snapshot); this lane confirmed the rendered type matches `formal.statement` and closed the fact by evidence only.
